Region: North Africa, west of Egypt (the Libya region)
History: Put, son of Ham (Genesis 10:6), is a North African people closely linked with the Libyans. The King James Version spells the name Phut in Genesis and Ezekiel and Put in Nahum. Put's warriors served in Tyre's army (Ezekiel 27:10), stood with Egypt's allies (Ezekiel 30:5; Nahum 3:9), and are named among Gog's coalition (Ezekiel 38:5). Beyond this warrior role, little is recorded of them.
Culture: Like their Libyan neighbors, the men of Put were known as soldiers and mercenaries in the armies of Tyre, Egypt, and the great powers.
Religion: Nothing distinct is recorded of Put's religion; as a North African people they shared the religious world of Libya and Egypt.
BibleConnection: Put appears only as a military ally in the prophets — with Tyre, with Egypt, and with Gog — a small people named wherever the great powers mustered their armies.
